destination.name: Lloyd Hotel (The Hoxton, Lloyd Amsterdam since 2023)
destination.note: No installed model or landmarks.json entry covered this pand; the OSM point n331837646 exists in click-poi-info.json and is reused as landmarkId.

facts: Designed by Evert Breman for the Koninklijke Hollandsche Lloyd; register dates the design 1917-1920, Wikipedia 1918-1921 (opened 1 June 1921); cost eight times the estimate.

Register: symmetric H-shaped plan, protruding central tower and two projecting end wings; souterrain, main floor, two further floors and an attic; central block under a hipped tiled roof, end wings under inset gabled tiled roofs; dormers with three-sided tops; eaves on corbels; brick facades with stone corner accents and cordon course, dark plinth.

Register: north front has, per storey on each side of the tower, two coupled pairs and one triple window with brick mullions; entrance with steps and a heavy canopy with coffered soffit carried on carved consoles.
Monument since 2001; hotel 2004-2021 (Lloyd Hotel), reopened 2023 as The Hoxton, Lloyd Amsterdam.

measuredBy.3dbag: NL.IMBAG.Pand.0363100012118149 LoD2.2: ground 1.449 m NAP, roofMax 27.42 NAP (tower dome), mansard-like main roof: 52-53 degree slopes from eave about 15 m to a flat top at 22.4 m; gabled wing roofs ridge about 22.9 m; flat annex roofs 3.7 m.
measuredBy.axisFrame: origin at the BAG centroid (4.9347433, 52.3742511); a along bearing 105.8 degrees, b to the right (south-south-west); core a -25.1..30.7, b -6.6..11.6; wing gables at b -11.6 (north) and b 14.4/14.3 (south); tower shaft a -0.7..6.1, b -9.4..-0.5.
measuredBy.heights: From ref-north.jpg (RCE 20409072; tower base about 36 px/m): plaque 6.2 m, shaft top 18.3, clock stage to 21.3, lantern to 23.9, dome tip 26.7 (3DBAG 26.0), vane about 29.
uncertain: The tower reads taller and heavier in the photographs than the 3DBAG dome height allows; the model follows 3DBAG, so it is visibly squatter than the reference.
Window sizes on the gable ends and the south front are read from oblique photographs; the east and west end walls and the annexes have no square-on photo (inferred).
Roof dormers are placed by eye, not counted.
